title: Role-Based Model Routing Evaluation
summary: Assign models to planner, executor, reviewer, researcher, and specialist roles only after testing the role contract and end-to-end workflow.
prerequisites: Per-step and terminal quality, safety, latency, and cost measures

sections.title: Define the role before choosing its model
paragraphs: A planner needs decomposition and constraint fidelity; an executor needs tool-contract accuracy and recovery behavior; a reviewer needs defect recall, evidence, and independence; a researcher needs source discipline; a specialist needs domain-specific acceptance criteria. Define required inputs, outputs, forbidden actions, budgets, and handoffs for each role.

Do not assign a provider or model from reputation alone. A less expensive model can be appropriate for a narrow structured transition while failing an ambiguous planning task, and a stronger model can add cost without improving a deterministic step.

sections.title: Evaluate transitions and terminal outcomes
paragraphs: Test each candidate on isolated role cases, then run the complete multi-role trajectory. Score instruction adherence, structured output, tool arguments, uncertainty, handoff completeness, reviewer defect detection, terminal correctness, safety, latency, and total cost.

Compare against a simple one-model baseline. Routing complexity is justified only when it improves declared outcomes enough to pay for more failure modes, state transitions, observability, and recovery paths.

code.label: Role routing experiment
code.code:
Task: [WORKFLOW AND ROUTING HYPOTHESIS]
Scope: [ROLES, CANDIDATE MODELS, TOOLS, DATA, AND ENVIRONMENT]
Permissions: [ROLE-SPECIFIC READ/WRITE/TOOL/AUTHORITY LIMITS]
Role contract: [INPUT -> REQUIRED OUTPUT -> FORBIDDEN ACTION -> HANDOFF]
Baseline and candidates: [ONE-MODEL BASELINE -> ROUTED OPTIONS]
Cases and metrics: [ROLE CASES + END-TO-END CASES -> THRESHOLDS]
Budgets: [TOKENS, TIME, COST, RETRIES, AND TOOL CALLS]
Stop conditions: [CRITICAL FAILURE, INVALID HANDOFF, LOOP, OR BUDGET]
Verification: [REPEATED RUNS, TRANSITION REVIEW, TERMINAL POSTCONDITION]
Recovery: [FALL BACK TO VERIFIED ROUTE, CHECKPOINT STATE, AND REPLAY SAFELY]

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: Expected evidence includes versioned role contracts, exact model configurations, a one-model baseline, isolated and end-to-end results, handoff and tool trajectories, slice metrics, budgets, and a routing decision with owner and expiry. Verify the terminal user outcome as well as each role's score.

Stop when a role exceeds authority, a handoff loses required context, the loop cannot converge, a critical case regresses, or routing cost exceeds its threshold. Recover by restoring the last verified route and prompt set, reconciling external actions, and replaying only idempotent or compensated transitions.

sections.title: Fixed-v1 worked case with traceable route decisions
paragraphs: This read-only simulation has two evaluator-owned cases. case1 is 3 plus 5 with trusted total 8 and is not critical. case2 is 12 plus 4 with trusted total 16 and is critical. An accepted route must submit each case exactly once and preserve every role contract through the terminal result.

The planner receives caseId, left, and right and must hand off caseId, operation, left, and right. It cannot execute arithmetic, omit an operand, or grant authority. The executor receives the complete plan and returns caseId, total, and toolCallCount. It cannot change the operation, use undeclared tools, or grant authority. The researcher returns procedure status and source URLs without altering arithmetic. The reviewer checks the plan, executor result, and researcher result. It cannot execute tools, grant permission, rewrite results, or approve missing evidence.

The baseline-1model and mixed-roles-1 fixtures pass with two complete trajectories out of two. cheap-critical-failure returns 17 for critical case2, so it has one complete trajectory out of two and is rejected. invalid-handoff omits right from the case1 plan and is rejected. over-budget has correct terminal results but uses 901 tokens against an upper budget of 900 and is rejected. authority-exceedance attempts to grant permission and is rejected. Reviewer metrics do not override any of these trajectory gates.

Each result summary includes the fixture aggregate usage, its upper budgets, and explicit failure reasons. These fields permit transparent route comparison without implying that the aggregate is measured per-role telemetry. Candidate labels are illustrative and establish no availability, license, price, quality, or ranking.

sections.title: Learner task: evaluate a changed input before viewing the key
paragraphs: Before reading the answer key, run the fixed replay, then run the changed fixture. The changed suite replaces the two fixed cases with one independent case: learner-case-1 has left 14, right 9, and trusted total 23. Predict how the terminal denominator and output change.

Trace these decisions: whether the planner includes both operands; whether the executor preserves operation add and returns 23; whether the researcher leaves the arithmetic unchanged; whether the reviewer checks the plan, executorResult, and researcherResult without executing a tool or granting permission; and whether the terminal output contains exactly one known result.

The changed fixture is not accepted by reusing the fixed suite's case IDs or aggregate. The evaluator selects a separate trusted case table for changed-v1. Adding learner-case-1 to a fixed-v1 document remains an unknown-case error.

code.label: Changed-input learner fixture definition
code.code:
{
  "suite": "changed-v1",
  "case": {"caseId": "learner-case-1", "left": 14, "right": 9, "trustedTotal": 23, "critical": true},
  "requiredTrace": [
    "planner handoff includes caseId, operation, left, and right",
    "executor returns total 23",
    "researcher does not alter arithmetic",
    "reviewer checks evidence without tool execution or permission grants",
    "terminal result contains learner-case-1 exactly once"
  ]
}

sections.title: Independent changed-v1 task and answer key
paragraphs: Before viewing the key, evaluate changed-v1 independently. It contains only learner-case-1, with left 14, right 9, trusted total 23, and critical true. Do not append it to fixed-v1 or reuse the fixed-v1 denominator.

Trace five decisions: the planner must include caseId learner-case-1, operation add, left 14, and right 9; the executor must preserve the operation and return 23; the researcher must not alter arithmetic; the reviewer must check plan, executorResult, and researcherResult without executing a tool or granting permission; and the terminal output must contain learner-case-1 exactly once.

Answer key: 14 plus 9 equals 23. The complete trajectory therefore passes 1 trusted case out of 1. The changed suite has one evaluator-owned reviewer probe, so successful detection gives denominator 1, one true positive, no false negative, no false positive, and recall 1.0. This is a contract result. Actual model behavior remains UNKNOWN until a dated, reproducible execution is recorded.

sections.title: Runnable standard-library offline replay
paragraphs: Save the code below as routing_replay.py. It uses only Python standard-library modules and performs no model API or model tool calls. Run `python routing_replay.py --write-fixtures` to create fixtures/fixed_replay.json, fixtures/changed_replay.json, and fixtures/negative_mutations.json. Then run `python routing_replay.py fixtures/fixed_replay.json`, `python routing_replay.py fixtures/changed_replay.json`, and `python routing_replay.py --test`.

The test command preserves artifacts under the caller-owned lab/routing-replay-tests directory and does not use an operating-system temporary directory. Its eight invalid documents exercise malformed top-level data, missing cases, duplicate cases, unknown cases, non-string case IDs, a negative executor tool-call count, invalid expectedDecision shape, and altered evaluator-owned injected truth. The validator also rejects empty or duplicate probe IDs and empty or duplicate defect IDs within a probe.

Both reviewer regressions invoke the full evaluate function with complete case trajectories, usage data, budgets, expected decisions, and evaluator-owned probe contracts. The swapped-report route returns REJECT with true positives 0, false negatives 2, false positives 2, denominator 2, and recall 0.0. The repeated-defect route returns REJECT with true positives 1, false negatives 1, false positives 0, denominator 2, and recall 0.5. reportedDefects remain observations, so misses and unknown reports reach metric computation instead of being rejected as malformed truth.

Expected test output is `TESTS PASS: 8 invalid documents rejected; 2 reviewer regressions passed; fixed and changed expectations matched`. This string is expected from the deterministic script. It is not a claim that the script was executed while drafting this material.

sections.title: Reviewer metrics, evaluator-owned truth, and route gates
paragraphs: Reviewer quality is computed from (probeId, defectId) pairs. For each probe, the evaluator forms injected pairs from injectedDefects and reported pairs from reportedDefects. True positives are pairs in both sets. False negatives are injected pairs not reported. False positives are reported pairs not injected. The denominator is the number of injected pairs, and recall is true positives divided by the denominator. In rendered results, trueDefects and injectedDefects both describe the amount of evaluator-owned truth, while recalledDefects and truePositives describe detections. These concepts must not be treated as interchangeable.

Consider two probes. probeone injects A and reports B, while probetwo injects B and reports A. Pair-aware scoring gives 0 true positives, 2 false negatives, 2 false positives, denominator 2, and recall 0.0. Flattening defect names would incorrectly produce recall 1.0 and 0 false positives. If both probes inject A but only probeone reports A, pair-aware scoring gives 1 true positive, 1 false negative, 0 false positives, denominator 2, and recall 0.5.

Probe identifiers, required probe coverage, and injected defects are evaluator-owned. Submitted reportedDefects are untrusted observations. They may be empty or contain unknown defect identifiers, which become misses or false positives rather than input-validation errors. Removing a required probe or changing injected truth fails validation and cannot improve the score. Probe IDs must be nonempty and unique. Defect IDs must be nonempty and unique within each list. Reusing the same defect ID in different probes is valid because each probe-defect pair is distinct.

Terminal success is the number of complete successful trajectories divided by the evaluator-owned trusted case count. It is not a sum of planner, executor, reviewer, or researcher scores. Missing, duplicate, unknown, or malformed cases fail validation. Critical failures, invalid handoffs, reviewer authority violations, reviewer misses, reviewer false positives, and budget exceedances are independent rejection gates.

Usage and budget objects contain exactly tokens, latencyMilliseconds, costUnits, retries, and toolCalls. Every value must be finite and nonnegative. Tokens, latencyMilliseconds, retries, and toolCalls must be integers and not booleans. executorResult.toolCallCount is also a nonnegative integer. It measures the executor subset, while route usage.toolCalls is the fixture aggregate for the complete route, so the evaluator requires the aggregate to be at least the sum of executor counts. expectedDecision is validated as a string before membership testing, preventing list-valued or dictionary-valued input from causing an uncontrolled set-membership error.

The evaluation procedure is provider-neutral. OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic document multi-agent workflow mechanisms at https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/multi-agent/ , https://adk.dev/workflows/ , and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents . These first-party references support the general workflow concepts, not the fictional candidate measurements in this exercise.

sections.title: Transfer the procedure without transferring fictional results
paragraphs: Replace the illustrative labels with deployment-owned identifiers and exact configurations. Candidate sets may include identifiers associated by the deployment owner with MetaLlama, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Phi, NVIDIA, Z.ai, and major hosted families. Do not infer availability, license, price, quality, or rank from inclusion in that list.

Preserve the evaluator-owned authority contract when changing candidates. In particular, reviewer output cannot grant tool permission, planner output cannot remove required executor inputs, and a route declaration cannot override a critical failure or budget exceedance.

The listed source URLs are procedure pointers for multi-agent workflow concepts. They are not blanket evidence for the fictional benchmark records, candidate assignments, arithmetic outcomes, costs, latency, availability, licenses, or comparative claims in this exercise.

sections.title: Verification status and source boundaries
paragraphs: The worked evidence record, candidate assignments, metrics, costs, latencies, retries, tool calls, and outcomes are fictional simulation values. They are included to make the procedure and arithmetic testable, not as observed benchmark results.

The cited first-party documentation supports the described software interfaces and general multi-agent workflow concepts. It does not support the fictional benchmark values or prove that any candidate assignment is available, licensed, or superior.

UNKNOWN: actual model outputs, actual provider availability, actual license terms, actual production cost, actual latency, actual retry count, actual tool-call count, and actual route quality. Establish these with dated primary evaluation data, exact configurations, reproducible fixtures, and recorded executions.

sections.title: Verification, unknowns, and provider-neutral transfer
paragraphs: The fixed and changed records are fictional fixtures for teaching evaluation mechanics. No live model execution, API call, external replay, provider comparison, confidence interval, or measured per-role telemetry is claimed. The arithmetic and expected decisions are determined by the supplied evaluator-owned contracts.

Actual model outputs, provider availability, license terms, production cost, production latency, retry counts, tool-call counts, and route quality are UNKNOWN. Establish them with dated primary records, exact model and prompt configurations, immutable fixtures, recorded trajectories, repeated executions, and separately captured per-role telemetry.

To transfer this method, replace illustrative candidate labels while preserving role inputs, outputs, forbidden actions, handoffs, trusted case tables, probe coverage, injected truth, terminal postconditions, usage scope, budgets, and rejection gates. A result claim must never redefine evaluator-owned truth, remove a failed probe, or override a critical trajectory failure.

The first-party workflow references are the OpenAI Agents SDK multi-agent guide at https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-js/guides/multi-agent/ , Google ADK workflow documentation at https://adk.dev/workflows/ , and Anthropic Claude subagent documentation at https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents . They are procedure references only and do not substantiate the fictional measurements or candidate assignments.
